playbook.position: Visiting-consultant revenue share stays within the standard band of 40-55% of net collections, reflecting specialty, consumable cost and OT overhead recovery.
International-facilitator commission stays within the standard band of 12-18% of gross billing, payable only once the Hospital has actually collected the patient's bill.
Cap proportionate to annual contract value, typically 1x-2x annual spend — not a flat token amount irrespective of contract size.

Mutual and capped. Counterparty indemnifies the hospital for its own acts; hospital indemnifies counterparty only for hospital-caused negligence (e.g. equipment failure, staff error), not a one-sided obligation.
Hospital retains a no-cause exit with 90-180 days' written notice and pro-rata settlement, in addition to for-cause termination with immediate effect on breach, licence loss or misconduct.
Courts at Ernakulam, Kerala for litigation; where arbitration is used, seat and venue at Kochi under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

Any counterparty accessing patient or personal data must have a DPDP Act 2023-compliant clause: purpose limitation, breach notification within 72 hours, and data return/deletion within 30 days of termination.
Standard 30 days from invoice or collection, as applicable. 45 days may be accepted for large capital purchases; anything beyond that needs Finance sign-off.
No silent auto-renewal beyond one term without written confirmation; hospital must get at least 60 days' notice before a renewal window closes, with a clear opt-out mechanism.

Maximum 1 year, narrowly scoped to directly competing NABH-accredited facilities within a reasonable radius — not a blanket district- or state-wide bar (restraint-of-trade risk under Contract Act s.27).

Counterparty must carry adequate professional indemnity / public liability / cyber insurance for the risk involved, with the hospital named as additional insured where the counterparty works on hospital premises.

Hospital retains the right to audit records, compliance and (where data is processed) security controls on reasonable notice, at least once a year, without needing the counterparty's consent each time.

contracts.title: Visiting consultant agreement — Dr. Divya Warrier, Interventional Cardiology

clauses.heading: TERM
clauses.text: This agreement is for a period of 3 years from the date of signing, renewable by mutual written consent.

clauses.heading: REVENUE SHARE
clauses.text: Hospital shall pay the Consultant 62% of net collections from interventional cardiology procedures performed by the Consultant, payable within 30 days of collection.
clauses.risk: Revenue share of 62% is well above the standard band of 40-55% for visiting consultants, eroding the hospital's margin on high-cost consumables and OT overheads.
clauses.redline: Revise to a tiered structure (e.g. 55% below a monthly volume threshold, 45% above it) or cap at 50% of net collections.

clauses.heading: INDEMNITY
clauses.text: The Consultant shall indemnify the Hospital against all claims arising from the Consultant's professional acts. The Hospital shall have no obligation to indemnify the Consultant under any circumstances.
clauses.risk: One-sided indemnity: the Consultant bears all risk while the Hospital carries zero indemnity obligation even for its own equipment failure or staff negligence.
clauses.redline: Make mutual: Hospital indemnifies the Consultant for Hospital-caused equipment/staff negligence, capped at a reasonable multiple of annual revenue share.

clauses.heading: NON-COMPETE
clauses.text: The Consultant shall not practice interventional cardiology at any other NABH-accredited hospital within a 5 km radius of this Hospital for a period of 1 year after termination of this agreement.

clauses.heading: EQUIPMENT & OT ACCESS
clauses.text: The Consultant shall have priority use of scheduled OT slots for interventional cardiology procedures, subject to the Hospital's OT allocation policy.

clauses.heading: CREDENTIALING
clauses.text: The Consultant shall maintain valid medical registration and Hospital credentialing/privileging for the duration of this agreement, and shall notify the Hospital immediately of any change in licence status.

clauses.heading: TERMINATION
clauses.text: Either party may terminate this agreement with 90 days' written notice.
clauses.risk: Only no-cause termination exists; there is no immediate-effect exit for licence suspension or misconduct, forcing the Hospital to run out the full notice period even in a serious case.
clauses.redline: Add an immediate-termination clause for licence suspension, criminal conviction, or a finding of professional misconduct.

clauses.heading: CONFIDENTIALITY
clauses.text: The Consultant shall keep confidential all non-public information of the Hospital, including patient data accessed in the course of practice, and shall not disclose it to any third party.
clauses.risk: Confidentiality is stated generally but there is no DPDP Act 2023-specific clause covering purpose limitation, breach notification, or post-termination data return/deletion for the patient data the Consultant accesses.
clauses.redline: Add a DPDP-compliant data processing clause: purpose limitation, 72-hour breach notification, and data return/deletion within 30 days of termination.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW & JURISDICTION
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of India, with courts at Ernakulam, Kerala having exclusive jurisdiction.

clauses.heading: INSURANCE
clauses.risk: No professional indemnity insurance requirement on the Consultant, leaving the Hospital exposed if a claim exceeds what the Consultant can personally satisfy.
clauses.redline: Add a requirement for professional indemnity insurance of at least ₹1 crore, with proof furnished annually.

missingClauses.note: No DPDP Act 2023-compliant clause for the patient data the Consultant accesses in the course of practice.
No separate for-cause, immediate-effect termination alongside the no-cause notice clause.
No professional indemnity insurance obligation on the Consultant.

contracts.title: Equipment lease / reagent rental — Sunrise Labtech Solutions (chemiluminescence immunoassay analyser)

clauses.heading: TERM
clauses.text: Lease of one (1) chemiluminescence immunoassay analyser for 3 years, with reagent rental (cost-per-test) pricing model.

clauses.heading: MINIMUM COMMITMENT
clauses.text: Hospital commits to a minimum of 38,000 tests per year; any shortfall is billed at the full reagent rate regardless of actual utilisation.
clauses.risk: No tolerance band — a slow quarter (e.g. a competing lab tie-up) results in full-rate billing on tests never run.
clauses.redline: Add a 15% shortfall tolerance before penal billing; true up annually, not per quarter.

clauses.heading: MAINTENANCE & SLA
clauses.text: Vendor shall provide preventive maintenance quarterly. Breakdown response time is best-effort, with no SLA specified.
clauses.risk: This analyser is critical-path for OPD/IPD reporting; an undefined response time risks reporting delays with no contractual recourse.
clauses.redline: Add an SLA: 4-hour response, 24-hour resolution, >=95% uptime guarantee with service credits below threshold.

clauses.heading: PRICE ESCALATION
clauses.text: Reagent pricing may be revised annually by the Vendor at its sole discretion.
clauses.risk: Open-ended cost exposure over a 3-year term with no ceiling on annual increases.
clauses.redline: Cap escalation at 5% p.a. or CPI/WPI-linked, whichever is lower.

clauses.heading: LIABILITY
clauses.text: Vendor's total liability under this agreement shall not exceed 1.5 times the annual contract value, irrespective of the cause of loss.

clauses.heading: EXIT
clauses.text: Hospital may not terminate before completion of 3 years except for Vendor's uncured material breach, with a 6-month cure period.
clauses.risk: Hospital is locked in for the full term even if a better-value vendor emerges, with no convenience exit at all.
clauses.redline: Add a convenience termination after year 2, with 6 months' notice and pro-rata settlement.

clauses.heading: TITLE & RETURN
clauses.text: Title to the equipment remains with the Vendor throughout the lease term. On expiry or termination, the Hospital shall permit removal within 30 days, subject to settlement of outstanding dues.

clauses.heading: DATA & LIS INTEGRATION

clauses.redline: Add a DPDP-compliant data processing addendum covering purpose limitation, access control and data return/deletion.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW

clauses.risk: Forces the Hospital to litigate outside Kerala for a Kochi-based dispute — high cost and inconvenience.
clauses.redline: Amend to Kerala law, courts at Ernakulam.

clauses.heading: FORCE MAJEURE
clauses.text: Neither party shall be liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided the affected party gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to mitigate.

missingClauses.note: No DPDP-compliant addendum despite LIS/patient-data integration.
No uptime/SLA reporting obligation to allow the Hospital to audit vendor performance against a defined standard.

clauses.text: Vendor shall process patient data solely to provide the Services, in accordance with its general privacy policy.

clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of India, with disputes referred to arbitration seated at Kochi under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

clauses.text: Spare parts above ₹25,000 per item are billed separately at the Vendor's then-current price list, at the Vendor's sole discretion on availability.
clauses.risk: "Sole discretion on availability" pricing for high-value parts creates open-ended cost exposure and a possible hold-up if a critical part is delayed.
clauses.redline: Fix a parts price list for the contract term, or cap the mark-up over cost.

clauses.heading: ESCALATION
clauses.text: CMC value may be revised at renewal, capped at 5% over the prior year's value.

clauses.heading: LIABILITY
clauses.text: Vendor's liability for direct loss arising from its negligence is capped at the annual CMC value; consequential losses are excluded by both parties.

clauses.heading: TERMINATION
clauses.text: Either party may terminate with 60 days' written notice, or with immediate effect for uncured material breach following a 30-day cure period.

clauses.heading: AUDIT & REPORTING
clauses.risk: No obligation on the Vendor to report service metrics, making it hard for the Hospital to verify SLA compliance without a dispute.
clauses.redline: Add a quarterly service-report obligation and an audit right over maintenance logs.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of India, with disputes referred to arbitration seated at Delhi.
clauses.risk: Arbitration seat is set at Delhi rather than Kochi, adding cost and inconvenience for a Kerala-based dispute.
clauses.redline: Amend the arbitration seat and venue to Kochi.

missingClauses.note: No uptime guarantee or service-credit mechanism on a critical clinical asset.
No quarterly reporting or audit right over maintenance logs.

contracts.title: Visiting consultant agreement — Dr. Divya Warrier, Bariatric Surgery

clauses.heading: TERM
clauses.text: This agreement is for a period of 2 years from the date of signing, renewable by mutual written consent.

clauses.heading: REVENUE SHARE
clauses.text: Hospital shall pay the Consultant 70% of net collections from bariatric surgery procedures performed by the Consultant, payable within 60 days of collection.
clauses.risk: Revenue share of 70% is well above the standard band of 40-55% for visiting consultants, eroding the hospital's margin on high-cost consumables and OT overheads.
clauses.redline: Revise to a tiered structure (e.g. 55% below a monthly volume threshold, 45% above it) or cap at 50% of net collections.

clauses.heading: PAYMENT (cont.)
clauses.text: Payment beyond the 60-day cycle noted above applies to all revenue-share disbursements without exception.
clauses.risk: Standard payment terms are 30 days; 60 days is a cash-flow drag on the Consultant relationship and an outlier versus other visiting-consultant agreements.
clauses.redline: Amend to 30 days of collection, or 45 days at most with Finance sign-off.

clauses.heading: INDEMNITY
clauses.text: The Consultant shall indemnify the Hospital against all claims arising from the Consultant's professional acts. The Hospital shall have no obligation to indemnify the Consultant under any circumstances.
clauses.risk: One-sided indemnity: the Consultant bears all risk while the Hospital carries zero indemnity obligation even for its own equipment failure or staff negligence.
clauses.redline: Make mutual: Hospital indemnifies the Consultant for Hospital-caused equipment/staff negligence, capped at a reasonable multiple of annual revenue share.

clauses.heading: NON-COMPETE
clauses.text: The Consultant shall not practice bariatric surgery at any other hospital within Ernakulam district for a period of 1 years after termination of this agreement.
clauses.risk: A district-wide, multi-year non-compete is a blanket restraint of trade likely unenforceable under Contract Act s.27 (Percept D'Mark v. Zaheer Khan line of authority); litigation risk if challenged.
clauses.redline: Narrow to 1 year, limited to directly competing NABH-accredited hospitals within a defined radius, not a district-wide bar.

clauses.heading: EQUIPMENT & OT ACCESS
clauses.text: The Consultant shall have priority use of scheduled OT slots for bariatric surgery procedures, subject to the Hospital's OT allocation policy.

clauses.heading: CREDENTIALING
clauses.text: The Consultant shall maintain valid medical registration and Hospital credentialing/privileging for the duration of this agreement, and shall notify the Hospital immediately of any change in licence status.

clauses.heading: TERMINATION
clauses.text: Either party may terminate this agreement with 120 days' written notice.
clauses.risk: Only no-cause termination exists; there is no immediate-effect exit for licence suspension or misconduct, forcing the Hospital to run out the full notice period even in a serious case.
clauses.redline: Add an immediate-termination clause for licence suspension, criminal conviction, or a finding of professional misconduct.

clauses.heading: CONFIDENTIALITY
clauses.text: The Consultant shall keep confidential all non-public information of the Hospital, including patient data accessed in the course of practice, and shall not disclose it to any third party.
clauses.risk: Confidentiality is stated generally but there is no DPDP Act 2023-specific clause covering purpose limitation, breach notification, or post-termination data return/deletion for the patient data the Consultant accesses.
clauses.redline: Add a DPDP-compliant data processing clause: purpose limitation, 72-hour breach notification, and data return/deletion within 30 days of termination.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW & JURISDICTION
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of India, with courts at Ernakulam, Kerala having exclusive jurisdiction.

clauses.heading: INSURANCE
clauses.text: The Consultant shall maintain professional indemnity insurance of not less than ₹1 crore for the duration of this agreement and shall furnish proof on request.

missingClauses.note: No DPDP Act 2023-compliant clause for the patient data the Consultant accesses in the course of practice.
No separate for-cause, immediate-effect termination alongside the no-cause notice clause.

contracts.title: International facilitator agreement — Continental Health Bridge

clauses.heading: APPOINTMENT
clauses.text: Hospital appoints the Facilitator on a non-exclusive basis to refer international patients from Central and East Africa for treatment at the Hospital.

clauses.heading: COMMISSION
clauses.text: Facilitator shall receive a commission of 12% of the gross billed amount for each referred patient who completes treatment at the Hospital.

clauses.heading: PAYMENT TIMING
clauses.text: Commission is payable within 30 days of the Hospital actually collecting the patient's bill in full.

clauses.heading: ANTI-KICKBACK / PATIENT INTEREST
clauses.text: Facilitator's dealings with patients are its own responsibility; the Hospital makes no representation as to the Facilitator's conduct with patients.
clauses.risk: No safeguard against the Facilitator double-charging patients or steering treatment choices for commission — a reputational and (in some destination countries) regulatory risk that can attach to the Hospital by association.
clauses.redline: Add a clause prohibiting patient-side charges for the referral and requiring disclosure of the commission arrangement on request.

clauses.heading: MARKETING MATERIALS
clauses.text: Facilitator may use Hospital-approved marketing materials only, and shall not make clinical claims not authorised in writing by the Hospital's Marketing department.

clauses.heading: DATA SHARING
clauses.text: Facilitator may share patient enquiry details (including passport copies and medical history) with the Hospital by email as needed for coordination.
clauses.risk: Patient medical history and identity documents moving by plain email, with no data-minimisation or retention limit, is a DPDP-relevant gap on both sides of the relationship.
clauses.redline: Add a DPDP-compliant data-handling undertaking with a secure channel and defined retention limit.

clauses.heading: TERM & TERMINATION
clauses.text: This agreement runs for 2 year(s) and may be terminated by either party with 90 days' written notice, or immediately for a breach of the anti-kickback/patient-interest clause.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of India, with disputes subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the Facilitator's home jurisdiction.
clauses.risk: Ceding jurisdiction to the Facilitator's home country makes enforcement (e.g. of the anti-kickback clause) impractical for the Hospital.
clauses.redline: Amend to Indian law with arbitration seated at Kochi.

clauses.heading: CURRENCY & TAX
clauses.text: Commission is payable in Indian Rupees, net of applicable TDS, within the timeline set out above.

missingClauses.note: No anti-kickback / patient-interest safeguard — reputational and regulatory exposure by association.
Patient documents shared by plain email with no data-handling undertaking.

contracts.title: Clinical establishment lease — Kavya Estates Pvt Ltd (Kaloor outpatient centre)

clauses.heading: PREMISES & USE
clauses.text: Landlord leases the ground-plus-3 building at Kaloor, Kochi, admeasuring approx. 42,000 sq ft, for use exclusively as a clinical establishment (outpatient centre and day-care procedures) under this Hospital's brand.

clauses.heading: TERM
clauses.text: Lease term of 15 years from the commencement date, with a lock-in period of 3 years during which the Hospital may not exit except for the Landlord's breach.

clauses.heading: RENT & ESCALATION
clauses.text: Monthly rent of ₹9.5 lakh, escalating at 12% every 3 years.
clauses.risk: 12% triennial escalation is above the typical 5-8% band for comparable Kochi clinical premises.
clauses.redline: Negotiate escalation down to 5-8% per 3-year block, or link to a published rent index.

clauses.heading: REGISTRATION & STAMP DUTY
clauses.text: The parties may execute this lease as an unregistered document notarised before a notary public.
clauses.risk: A 15-year lease exceeding 1 year must be registered to be enforceable in court; an unregistered document weakens the Hospital's position on any future dispute over possession or terms.
clauses.redline: Require registration under the Registration Act, 1908.

clauses.heading: STRUCTURAL & FIT-OUT
clauses.text: Hospital may carry out structural modifications required for clinical licensing (fire safety, biomedical waste storage, oxygen pipeline) subject to Landlord's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

clauses.heading: SUBLEASE & ASSIGNMENT
clauses.text: Hospital may permit specific clinical departments or empanelled diagnostic partners to operate from the premises under its overall licence, without requiring fresh Landlord consent for each such arrangement.

clauses.heading: MAINTENANCE
clauses.text: Landlord is responsible for structural repairs and common-area maintenance; the Hospital is responsible for interior fit-out and equipment maintenance.

clauses.heading: TERMINATION FOR CAUSE
clauses.text: Either party may terminate immediately for the other's uncured material breach following 60 days' written notice and opportunity to cure.

clauses.heading: INSURANCE
clauses.text: Hospital shall maintain fire and special-perils insurance covering its fit-out and equipment; Landlord shall maintain building insurance for the structure.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW
clauses.text: This lease is governed by the laws of Kerala, with courts at Ernakulam having exclusive jurisdiction.

missingClauses.note: Lease exceeds 1 year but is proposed as unregistered — enforceability risk.

contracts.title: NDA — Meridian Biosciences Sponsor Trust (an investigator-initiated diagnostics validation study)

clauses.heading: PURPOSE
clauses.text: This Non-Disclosure Agreement is entered into in connection with discussions for an investigator-initiated diagnostics validation study at the Hospital, sponsored by Meridian Biosciences Sponsor Trust.

clauses.heading: CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATION
clauses.text: The Hospital shall keep confidential all information disclosed by the Sponsor. The Sponsor has no reciprocal confidentiality obligation toward information disclosed by the Hospital (e.g. site capability, patient volume data).
clauses.risk: A one-way NDA leaves the Hospital's own disclosures (site data, capability information) unprotected, which is unusual and unfavourable for a bilateral research relationship.
clauses.redline: Make the confidentiality obligation mutual.

clauses.heading: CARVE-OUTS
clauses.text: The confidentiality obligation does not apply to information that is already public, independently developed, or required to be disclosed by law or a regulatory authority (including the Ethics Committee and CDSCO), provided notice is given where legally permissible.

clauses.heading: TERM & SURVIVAL
clauses.text: This NDA is effective for 3 years, with the confidentiality obligation surviving for 3 years after termination or expiry.

clauses.heading: PATIENT DATA
clauses.text: Any patient-identifiable information remains subject to the Hospital's own DPDP Act 2023 obligations and the study's Ethics Committee-approved protocol, independent of this NDA's general confidentiality terms.

clauses.heading: RETURN OR DESTRUCTION
clauses.text: On request or termination, each party shall return or certify destruction of the other's confidential information within 30 days, except for one archival copy retained for legal/regulatory record-keeping.

clauses.heading: NO LICENCE
clauses.text: Nothing in this NDA grants either party a licence to use the other's confidential information for any purpose other than evaluating and conducting the study.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of Kerala, with courts at Ernakulam having exclusive jurisdiction.

missingClauses.note: Confidentiality obligation is one-way; Hospital disclosures are unprotected.

contracts.title: Equipment lease / reagent rental — Coral Diagnostics Pvt Ltd (chemiluminescence immunoassay analyser)

clauses.heading: TERM
clauses.text: Lease of one (1) chemiluminescence immunoassay analyser for 5 years, with reagent rental (cost-per-test) pricing model.

clauses.heading: MINIMUM COMMITMENT
clauses.text: Hospital commits to a minimum of 32,000 tests per year, with a 15% shortfall tolerance before penal billing applies, trued up annually.

clauses.heading: MAINTENANCE & SLA
clauses.text: Vendor shall provide preventive maintenance quarterly. Breakdown response time is best-effort, with no SLA specified.
clauses.risk: This analyser is critical-path for OPD/IPD reporting; an undefined response time risks reporting delays with no contractual recourse.
clauses.redline: Add an SLA: 4-hour response, 24-hour resolution, >=95% uptime guarantee with service credits below threshold.

clauses.heading: PRICE ESCALATION
clauses.text: Reagent pricing may be revised annually by the Vendor at its sole discretion.
clauses.risk: Open-ended cost exposure over a 5-year term with no ceiling on annual increases.
clauses.redline: Cap escalation at 5% p.a. or CPI/WPI-linked, whichever is lower.

clauses.heading: LIABILITY
clauses.text: Vendor's total liability under this agreement shall not exceed ₹1,00,000 in aggregate, irrespective of the cause of loss.
clauses.risk: A flat ₹1 lakh cap is grossly disproportionate to a likely annual spend of ₹39 lakh at this volume — inadequate cover for a reporting-error or equipment-damage event.
clauses.redline: Raise the cap to 1x-2x annual contract value.

clauses.heading: EXIT
clauses.text: Hospital may not terminate before completion of 5 years except for Vendor's uncured material breach, with a 6-month cure period.
clauses.risk: Hospital is locked in for the full term even if a better-value vendor emerges, with no convenience exit at all.
clauses.redline: Add a convenience termination after year 2, with 6 months' notice and pro-rata settlement.

clauses.heading: TITLE & RETURN
clauses.text: Title to the equipment remains with the Vendor throughout the lease term. On expiry or termination, the Hospital shall permit removal within 30 days, subject to settlement of outstanding dues.

clauses.heading: DATA & LIS INTEGRATION
clauses.risk: The analyser integrates with the LIS and patient records; the agreement is silent on data-handling, access-control, or breach-notification terms.
clauses.redline: Add a DPDP-compliant data processing addendum covering purpose limitation, access control and data return/deletion.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of the state where the Vendor is headquartered (Pune), with courts at Pune having exclusive jurisdiction.
clauses.risk: Forces the Hospital to litigate outside Kerala for a Kochi-based dispute — high cost and inconvenience.
clauses.redline: Amend to Kerala law, courts at Ernakulam.

clauses.heading: FORCE MAJEURE
clauses.text: Neither party shall be liable for delay or failure caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided the affected party gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to mitigate.

missingClauses.note: No DPDP-compliant addendum despite LIS/patient-data integration.
No uptime/SLA reporting obligation to allow the Hospital to audit vendor performance against a defined standard.

contracts.title: CMC — cath lab imaging system (Apex CSSD Solutions)

clauses.heading: SCOPE
clauses.text: Comprehensive Maintenance Contract (CMC) covering the cath lab imaging system, including all preventive maintenance, breakdown calls, and software updates for 1 year(s).

clauses.heading: RESPONSE TIME
clauses.text: Vendor shall respond to a breakdown call within 24 hours during business hours (Mon-Sat, 9am-6pm).
clauses.risk: A 24-hour, business-hours-only response is inadequate for a critical diagnostic/imaging asset that runs emergency and inpatient cases outside those hours.
clauses.redline: Amend to a 4-8 hour response, 24x7, given the criticality of this asset.

clauses.heading: UPTIME GUARANTEE
clauses.risk: No uptime guarantee or service credit mechanism — downtime has no contractual consequence for the Vendor.
clauses.redline: Add a minimum 95% uptime guarantee with service credits for shortfall.

clauses.heading: SPARE PARTS
clauses.text: All spare parts and consumable components (excluding items under a separate reagent contract) are included within the CMC value.

clauses.heading: ESCALATION
clauses.text: CMC value may be revised at renewal, capped at 5% over the prior year's value.

clauses.heading: LIABILITY
clauses.text: Vendor's liability for direct loss arising from its negligence is capped at the annual CMC value; consequential losses are excluded by both parties.

clauses.heading: TERMINATION
clauses.text: Either party may terminate with 60 days' written notice, or with immediate effect for uncured material breach following a 30-day cure period.

clauses.heading: AUDIT & REPORTING
clauses.risk: No obligation on the Vendor to report service metrics, making it hard for the Hospital to verify SLA compliance without a dispute.
clauses.redline: Add a quarterly service-report obligation and an audit right over maintenance logs.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of India, with disputes referred to arbitration seated at Bangalore.
clauses.risk: Arbitration seat is set at Bangalore rather than Kochi, adding cost and inconvenience for a Kerala-based dispute.
clauses.redline: Amend the arbitration seat and venue to Kochi.

missingClauses.note: No uptime guarantee or service-credit mechanism on a critical clinical asset.
No quarterly reporting or audit right over maintenance logs.

contracts.title: Housekeeping outsourcing — Silverline Facility Services

clauses.heading: SCOPE & MANPOWER
clauses.text: Vendor shall deploy 52 trained housekeeping personnel across the Hospital campus on a 3-shift basis, per the roster agreed with Facilities/Administration.

clauses.heading: STATUTORY COMPLIANCE
clauses.text: Vendor shall pay all deployed personnel not less than the applicable Kerala minimum wage, remit PF/ESI contributions on time, and furnish monthly compliance proof (challans, wage registers) to the Hospital.

clauses.heading: SUPERVISION
clauses.text: Vendor shall provide one on-site supervisor per shift, responsible for quality checks, attendance, and escalation of incidents to the Hospital's Facilities/Security desk.

clauses.heading: INDEMNITY
clauses.text: Vendor indemnifies the Hospital against claims arising from acts of its personnel; the Hospital indemnifies the Vendor only for loss caused by the Hospital's own instructions to Vendor staff, subject to a cap of one year's contract value.

clauses.heading: INSURANCE
clauses.text: Vendor shall maintain insurance "as required by law".
clauses.risk: No specified insurance amount or requirement to name the Hospital as additional insured — a generic "as required by law" clause offers little practical protection.
clauses.redline: Specify workmen's compensation for all deployed staff and public liability of at least ₹50 lakh, Hospital named as additional insured.

clauses.heading: TERMINATION
clauses.text: Either party may terminate this agreement with 30 days' written notice, or with immediate effect for a serious breach (e.g. repeated statutory non-compliance, a security lapse causing harm).

clauses.heading: AUDIT
clauses.risk: No explicit audit right over the Vendor's compliance records or training logs.
clauses.redline: Add an audit right over compliance records, training logs and rosters on reasonable notice.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of Kerala, with courts at Ernakulam having exclusive jurisdiction.

contracts.title: IT SaaS — e-prescription & drug-interaction checker (NimbusHealth Systems)

clauses.heading: SCOPE
clauses.text: Vendor shall provide the e-prescription & drug-interaction checker module as a hosted, subscription (SaaS) add-on integrated with the Hospital's HIS via API, for 1 year(s).

clauses.heading: DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM
clauses.text: Vendor shall process patient data solely to provide the Services, in accordance with its general privacy policy.
clauses.risk: No DPDP-specific Data Processing Addendum — reliance on a generic privacy policy does not satisfy the Hospital's obligations as data fiduciary for patient personal data processed by this Vendor.
clauses.redline: Annex a DPDP-compliant DPA covering purpose limitation, processor obligations, and the Hospital's instructions as data fiduciary.

clauses.heading: DATA RESIDENCY
clauses.text: All patient data processed under this agreement shall be hosted on servers located within India.

clauses.heading: BREACH NOTIFICATION
clauses.text: The agreement does not specify a breach-notification timeline.
clauses.risk: DPDP Act practice expects breach notification within 72 hours; a non-binding target or silence leaves the Hospital unable to meet its own regulatory notification timelines.
clauses.redline: Set a binding 72-hour breach-notification obligation.

clauses.heading: SUB-PROCESSORS
clauses.text: Vendor may engage sub-processors at its discretion without notice to the Hospital.
clauses.risk: Undisclosed sub-processing of patient data removes the Hospital's ability to assess or object to additional parties handling patient information.
clauses.redline: Require a disclosed sub-processor list with 30 days' prior notice before any addition.

clauses.heading: SERVICE LEVEL
clauses.text: Vendor guarantees 99.5% monthly uptime, with service credits for shortfall, and shall notify the Hospital of planned downtime at least 48 hours in advance.

clauses.heading: FEES & AUTO-RENEWAL
clauses.text: Subscription fees are payable annually in advance. The Hospital will be notified at least 60 days before the renewal date and must actively confirm renewal in writing.

clauses.heading: EXIT & DATA RETURN
clauses.text: On termination or expiry, Vendor shall export all Hospital data in a usable format within 30 days and thereafter permanently delete it, certifying deletion in writing.

clauses.heading: LIABILITY
clauses.text: Vendor's aggregate liability under this agreement is capped at the fees paid in the preceding 12 months, except for liability arising from a data breach caused by the Vendor's negligence, which is uncapped.

clauses.heading: GOVERNING LAW
clauses.text: This agreement is governed by the laws of India, with courts at Ernakulam, Kerala having exclusive jurisdiction.

missingClauses.note: No DPDP-compliant Data Processing Addendum annexed.
